summary: Phase 149O.16.1 -- Publication Coordinator Python 3.9/3.10 Timestamp Compatibility Repair: narrow production repair of the single non-implementation prerequisite finding from 149O.16 (149O.12B-Obs-PY39-1). Ran the required initial inspection (git status/branch/log/rev-list, pcae health/check/status coherence/doctor task-memory/push check/runtime inspect, telegram notify status, phase-report show --latest) and confirmed the expected baseline: repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.16 completed/complete/pushed, HMRC-001 v1.0 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- CONFORMS, HATP production NOT READY, runtime Observed/observe/unavailable. Read pcae.governance.publication.coordinator._parse_timestamp and its two direct callers (_validate_authorization_freshness) directly and independently: confirmed bare datetime.fromisoformat(value) with no trailing-Z normalization, both call sites already wrapped in try/except ValueError -> StaleAuthorizationError. Confirmed pyproject.toml still declares requires-python >= 3.9 -- Python 3.9/3.10 remain supported, repair required. No Python 3.9/3.10 interpreter was available in this environment (only Python 3.14.5, no pyenv, no /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.9 or python3.10); on 3.14 datetime.fromisoformat already accepts a trailing Z natively (CPython 3.11+ behavior, bpo-41762), so a live pre-repair failure could not be triggered directly -- confirmed instead by direct source inspection, the documented version-gated stdlib change, and this repository's own three pre-existing, independently-authored test-layer monkeypatch workaround fixtures (test_hatp_signing_ceremony.py, test_phase_149o_12c_hsce_attack_matrix.py, test_phase_149o_13_...py) that had already reproduced and worked around the failure on this repo's .venv before this repair existed. Independently inspected the existing safe precedent, pcae.core.rollback_approval_evidence._parse_iso_timestamp (text = value[:-1] + '+00:00' if value.endswith('Z') else value, then fromisoformat(text)), and confirmed no other src/pcae/ parser shares this defect by direct inspection (not broadened by grep). Applied the narrowest repair: normalize a terminal 'Z' to '+00:00' immediately before fromisoformat inside _parse_timestamp, mirroring the RAE precedent exactly -- no wholesale parser replacement, no new dependency, no new timestamp format, no shared-helper refactor, no change to _now_iso() or canonical serialization. Verified semantic boundaries explicitly: terminal-Z-only normalization (interior Z untouched); uppercase-only (lowercase 'z' still rejected); existing '+00:00'/other-offset input unchanged (no double normalization, no UTC conversion of non-UTC offsets); fractional-second Z accepted with fractional precision preserved; invalid inputs (empty, malformed, double timezone suffix) still rejected; naive-timestamp coercion to UTC unchanged; identical ValueError error-mapping at both call sites. Authored a new 12-test file (tests/test_phase_149o_16_1_publication_coordinator_timestamp_compatibility_repair.py) exercising the real, unpatched production _parse_timestamp directly with no monkeypatch, including terminal-Z acceptance, Z/+00:00 instant equivalence, +00:00 non-regression, fractional-Z acceptance, non-UTC-offset non-regression, lowercase-z rejection, four invalid-input cases, a production-source-shape assertion, and a full end-to-end real CHGR Decision creation path (PublicationCoordinator.authorize -> execute) with Z-suffixed built_at/invoked_at succeeding. Demonstrated pre-repair attribution via git stash: with the production change reverted, the new source-shape assertion test fails (the only new-suite assertion this 3.14 interpreter's own native Z-acceptance cannot mask) while the rest pass -- documented as the available attribution proof given no 3.9/3.10 interpreter in this environment; repair restored, full new suite green again (12/12). Updated exactly two pre-existing tests whose own assertions the repair necessarily invalidated, per this repository's 149O.5-F-3 'update in place, never delete' convention: test_phase_149o_13_...py's own defect-reproduction test, which had asserted the pre-repair source shape as its evidence, now asserts the repaired shape and calls the real production function directly (renamed test_python39_z_suffix_defect_repaired_by_149o_16_1); test_phase_149o_12b_...py's TestProductionFileAllowlist, whose cumulative-diff-since-149O.12A-baseline allowlist did not yet include coordinator.py, now does, with a docstring note following the exact same 149O.12C/149O.5-F-3 precedent already documented in that file. Left all three historical monkeypatch workaround fixtures in place, unremoved -- now harmlessly idempotent, not required to prove repair consumption since the new no-monkeypatch test file proves it independently. Ran targeted regression across 144C, HATP signing ceremony, 149O.12B, 149O.12C, 149O.13, 149O.15, 149O.16, plus this phase's new file: 254 passed, 2 skipped, zero failures. Ran the fast_green baseline (pytest -m fast_green -k 149o, excluding the pre-existing fido2-dependent collection error): 256 passed, 2 skipped once this phase's commits landed (two pre-existing origin/main..HEAD-diff-based 'no production change' self-checks in 149O.15's and 149O.16's own suites transiently fail while this phase's commits are ahead of unpushed origin/main -- expected and resolved by this phase's own push, not a real regression; no edit made to either file). Authored the phase document, docs/PHASE_149O_16_1_PUBLICATION_COORDINATOR_PYTHON_39_310_TIMESTAMP_COMPATIBILITY_REPAIR.md, covering baseline, finding reconstruction, supported Python range, affected function/callers, pre-repair reproduction and its stated limitation, existing safe precedent, selected repair, all confirmed semantic boundaries, the CHGR/RAE path, production-diff classification, historical monkeypatch disposition, the two necessitated pre-existing-test updates, full test results, no-go confirmations, finding disposition, repair verdict, and recommended next phase. VERDICT: PUBLICATION TIMESTAMP PYTHON 3.9/3.10 COMPATIBILITY: REPAIRED -- READY FOR INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. 149O.12B-Obs-PY39-1: REPAIRED AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL -- PENDING INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. HMRC-001 v1.0 remains byte-unchanged and VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- CONFORMS. HSCE-001/HATP-001/RAE-001/PB contracts remain byte-unchanged. No HMRC-001 implementation was started. B-149O-1..4 remain INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AT HATP-GATED AUTHORITY BOUNDARY -- SYSTEM EXECUTION CLOSURE DEFERRED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Full detail in docs/PHASE_149O_16_1_PUBLICATION_COORDINATOR_PYTHON_39_310_TIMESTAMP_COMPATIBILITY_REPAIR.md.
